skill.displayName: 弱电智能化投标决策-安防监控项目投标评估

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its bid-analysis purpose, but it defaults to saving shareable reports that preserve login-bypass signed links and also persists account credentials.

dimensions.detail: Network calls to the provider API, reading user-provided bid files, and writing reports are proportionate for this skill; optional auto-registration collects platform, arch, and hashed MAC only after consent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The manifest only declares the ZLBX_API_KEY environment variable while the instructions also use ~/.zlbx/config.json and an included executable report renderer; these are disclosed in SKILL.md but not represented in metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The workflow is mostly scoped to specific intelligent-building/security bid decisions and includes API cost limits, but it mandates default HTML export and exact preservation of access-bearing signed links without a clear user opt-in for sharing-sensitive output.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes API keys to ~/.zlbx/config.json and defaults to storing HTML reports under ~/zlbx-bid-decision-files/, with report links required to retain signed sk parameters that may grant access to protected records.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Bid analysis, API querying, local report generation, and optional account setup are coherent with the stated purpose, but preserving signed sk URLs in shareable HTML reports is higher-risk than needed for ordinary evidence links.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with this provider receiving bid-search terms and optional device features for registration, and avoid sharing generated HTML reports unless you understand that they may contain signed access links. Prefer using a preconfigured API key and consider removing or redacting sk links before distributing reports outside your team.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Local reading of user-provided bid files and writing reports is explicitly disclosed and fits the workflow, though metadata does not fully express those file capabilities.
[TP4] expected: Branded HTML report generation and footer links are disclosed in the template and renderer; this is promotional but not hidden or unrelated to report output.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger text is broad within the intelligent-building/security-bid domain, but it still requires a concrete bid-decision or pricing-analysis intent rather than arbitrary security or monitoring requests.
[SQP-2] expected: Default HTML export is purpose-aligned, but because bid strategy can be sensitive, persisting a shareable report by default is a real review concern.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The artifact explicitly requires API-returned URLs with sk免登录签名 parameters to be preserved in reports and HTML; embedding those signed access links in shareable files is not necessary for the core analysis and creates access-leak risk.
[E1] expected: Auto-registration sends platform, CPU architecture, and a SHA-256 MAC hash to the provider only after user consent and is disclosed as a free-trial deduplication flow, but it remains sensitive host-fingerprint handling.
[E1] expected: The curl/requests examples operationalize the same consent-gated auto-registration flow rather than undisclosed exfiltration; the concern is downgraded to user-review guidance.
